text:
This KFC is next to BK and Black Bear Diner (across from Wienerschnitzel in Sparks). I used to eat Kentucky Fried Chicken as a kid and really liked it.  I'm still down with greasy fried chicken but damn I want that Popeye's back!!  Popeye's in the Western Addition neighborhood SF got me stuck on that greasy ass (terrible for you, but damn soooo good) flava.  KFC, judging by this Sparks location, and the "new" style chicken....oh man....my stomach just lurched up into my throat by the thought of it.

I mainly went there because Jr. Thirst wanted to go.  Sometimes eight-year-olds (he was @ the time anyway) can make surprisingly good calls on dining choices.  umm not UURRP this time by the way.  Holy God and Baby Jesus, dare I continue?

There was some kind of "bonus deal" (more on this later) that involved a literal ass-load of chicken.  Like a whole extra box o-chicken along with your regular 8 piece, or 10 piece, or whatnot.  OK you got me pricewise.  Gimme the usual sides of the biscuits and the cole slaw, and we're good.

Biscuits are dry but taste OK, like always.  That butter that comes in the nonrefrigerated packs is like chemical warfare material BTW.   ICK!  dip those mothers in the gravy or something, but don't use that warm, nonperishable butter substitute shit, whatever you do.

Cole slaw--I freaking LOVE KFC cole slaw.  Even after the upcoming (UURP) experience, I would still gladly eat any amount of KFC cole slaw.  It's always the same with the sweetness and that fake mayo sauce or whatever it is.  I wouldn't try to compare it to anybody's homemade stuff (or anything else fresh), but it's crunchy and juicy, and makes a great side.  Plus, after the next (EURGHH) experience, cole slaw will probably be the only thing I'll ever eat at any KFC again.  Period.

Long story short = ate about four good-sized pieces of chicken.  I eat a lot, so not a big deal for me usually.   Also had a couple small portions of the sides, I hadn't eaten all day...should be just what I needed.  I had eaten at this one before, actually I had taken it to go about three times, your typical fast food mediocrity, but pretty satisfying.  Last time (which was probably late 2008 or so) was a very different matter.

Before we even left the restaurant (20 minutes after the initial chicken ingestion) I started to feel dizzy and not right with the world.  Let's see...I'm sober (at that moment) and  with no major health issues, according to my doctor.  The only thing that I can compare the sensation to: about 20 years ago, after dating a girl who was vegetarian, I had been vegetarian for about six months after giving red meat up for about a year beforehand.  I visited my German grandma's house a day or two before Xmas, and she insisted on cooking  sausage from the German deli, despite me saying I was only going to have the potato and vegetable sides.  I ate about 2/3 of one veal-based, fatty sausage (which still tasted fresh and high-quality) and had to sit down.  I felt dizzy and slightly nauseated, retired to the guest room and passed out for over two hours.  To this day, I know that was my body not being used to producing the enzymes needed to break down meat (especially fatty meat).

But now I eat meat.  Lots of it.  Almost every meal contains meat.  And KFC still gave me that PHYSICALLY SICK feeling anyway.  At the time they were trying to promote some kind of "no trans fat" fad thing, so they might have been using a synthetic, weird shortening to deep fry their chicken.  Whatever the case, I had awful food-poisoning type symptoms (I'll spare the obvious details) for two days straight and felt like I was going to die.

Which brings me to the "bonus" chicken.  To steal a comparison that I heard years ago, getting "bonus" KFC chicken is like having a surgeon amputate a "bonus" limb when he goes in to remove a gangrenous infection.  sooo, if you're slow and still don't get it, WHY THE LIVING HELL WOULD I WANT LIKE 8 PIECES OF CHICKEN WHEN FOUR MADE ME FEEL LIKE I WAS GONNA CRAP AND VOMIT OUT MY ENTIRE DIGESTIVE SYSTEM??  It's like they're trying to get rid of that toxic crap.  I threw out all the chicken after getting home, but couldn't bring myself to dispose of the cole slaw.  After eating some slaw the next day and not getting a bad reaction, I can say it was definitely the chicken that  was to blame.

EECHHH, I can barely watch a KFC commercial even now.  And now they're promoting that supposedly heart-healthy "grilled" chicken.  

sorry KFC, some of us don't mind overly fatty foods, if they are done right, taste good, and don't make you sick.  Your attempt at prolonging my life(with that "no trans fat" grease you fried the chicken parts in) made me want to slit my wrists with a rusty razor, rather than undergo more gastric agony.  I can't bring myself to try any other chicken from y'all.  Just give me a lifetime supply of cole slaw, and I suppose I can call it even.

The last time we came here we said we wouldn't come back,  but as that was awhile ago, I went against that decision and decided to try it again.   MISTAKE. 

This has to be the loudest restaurant I've ever eaten in.   The last time,  we complained about the noise and were told "it's family style and people like to have a good time".  So it's perfectly acceptable to yell down the table to other people in your group and dance in the aisles, heck the staff will even laugh and clap along with you.  See they can laugh and clap along because they aren't using that time to actually provide you with good service.   Waitress disappeared so long we were asking other wait staff for things,  and those requests were mostly ignored.   This time we asked for a table in a quieter section of the restaurant,  the hostess smiled at us,  like YEAH RIGHT GOOD LUCK WITH THAT.   Once again we couldn't hear the people directly across the table from us, and my college aged kids went outside as soon as they were done their meal because of it.

On a plus side,  I noticed most people bringing like 12 packs of beer and lots of wine in.  it's byob even though they have a liquor license.  That probably accounts for some of the noise.  It's like an Eagles game with Italian food.  Except I didn't want to eat at an Eagles game,  I wanted a nice dinner with my family. 

And for all the people that complain about having reservations and still having to wait a long time,  I can confirm that's true and I know part of the reason.   As you wait for almost an hour past your reservation time you'll notice that the owner will seat everyone he knows before you, even though they don't have reservations.   See he's a great guy that way.   He'll also come around and socialize with those same people,  yet act like everyone else there is an annoyance to him. 

If you read thru the reviews you'll see these same things complained about over and over again.  And I can only guess that the people giving the good reviews are his friends that he takes care of,  and those individuals that love hitting the liquor store on the way to the restaurant so they can party it up "on the cheap"

Kind of a shame too, because the food is actually pretty good

So, this is definitely not my first time at Slice on Magazine, however this will definitely be my last. Not only did my roommates and I wait for an hour to pick up our pizza, which we were told would only take 20-25 minutes to be ready on a Thursday night around 8pm (we waited at the bar being ignored by the bartender for 20 minutes), when we finally got our cold pizza it turns out to have mystery ingredients, and I am not talking about Meatloaf Surprise in the Cafeteria of high schools on Wednesdays. I am talking sometimes your pizza might have freshly roasted garlic, but other times it may have dead moths. That's right, I said it DEAD MOTHS!!!!!!!!! So after waiting to get my pizza for an hour and then driving all the way home (5min drive) and sitting down to dinner with my roommates, just to find a dead moth in my pizza, which luckily my roommates did not immediately throw up their pizza. Luckily! So get back in the car after screaming because there was an unexpected moth, sort of caught me off guard. So driving back, I am thinking, these peeps are just going to return my money and offer to replace the pizza. That would be awesome, easy, done, and go home and eat. However, when I arrive back at the restaurant and immediately get the bartender's attention, I would rather not wait 20 minutes for him to even acknowledge my presence, but when I told him that there was a moth, he was just like " Ohhhh...somethings are just out of our control", and replaced the pizza. Somethings are out of your control? NO NO NO, unfortunately that is not how customer service works. I was absolutely repulsed by moth, first of all, but to be treated like this is a no big deal. NOPE! Sorry! The pizza was replaced, and to its credit I must say that the pizza is good, however, I will not be returning to Slice, not with the risk of getting another moth in my pizza. 

Also, if you decide to test your own luck (GOOD LUCK), try not to look into the kitchen area. It is absolutely repulsive to watch grown men pick up the ingredients they are placing on your pizza with their bare, sweaty, probably not the cleanest hands. If you are going to allow your kitchen to be that unsanitary, I would recommend putting up solid doors that are not able to be seen by the outside public. The place was an absolute mess, and honestly they looked short staffed and not super friendly. Overall, pizza good, staff unhelpful, and BEWARE OF MOTHS. 

PS: This is not the first time my roommate has encountered a problem with Slice on Magazine. When she went there was a piece of long (we are talking long like probably a good ways down the back) long black hair wrapped around her lettuce in her salad (my roommate has Red hair in case you were wondering). Like did you intentionally wrap a hair around it and give it out to the most innocent person you saw just to see if they would see it? Is that how you get your fun working at a dirty place that is probably a whole lot dirtier behind the scenes. 

We, my roommates and I, will be taking our business to Reginelli's, who you should take a note from on the Customer Service side. When they make a mistake, they are quick to replace it and even quicker to offer their customers some kind of compensation for their mistakes. But if you are looking for good pizza and awesome people who can admit when they have made a mistake and truly enjoy working in a clean and respectable establishment, GO TO REGINELLI's, not Slice.  I repeat NOT SLICE. Not only will you get a better price, but you won't be afraid to find moths or hair in your food. Good luck in your food adventures and remember Reginelli's over Slice any day and everyday.

I WAS a frequent eater at properly fueled mainly due to my gluten sensitivities and allergies. Those of you who know me even recommended this place even posts on Facebook. I will no longer dine here not because of the food, but because of the way the handled a miscommunication between myself and staff. As I approached the register I asked for some gluten free bread with hummus. The lady behind the register said "you mean a hummus sandwich" and I said with hesitation yes I guess... can I just have some avocado with it. As they do have avocado smash as well as an order of hummus. She saw I didn't look at the menu. When the order came out it was a full sandwich with tomatoes carrots onions etc. I have an allergy to carrots and was not expecting a full sandwich more like hummus and avocado on gluten free bread.  What proceeded next for someone who frequents the there was sooooo ludicrous. The lady behind the register said that I would have to pay for
another sandwich. I asked to speak with the owner since she knows me and I'm there a lot. Her daughter came out who also knew me as we had discussions before didn't even say hello,
And said you knew it was on the menu and proceeded to argue with me. I said it was a misunderstanding but I shouldn't have to pay and she insisted. She even put words in my mouth saying "since you are saying it's her fault" which I never said it was the staffs fault, it was a misunderstanding. What a shame they would treat a regular customer like that. Because I was going to stay and do some work there, I decided to leave and go some where else as I prefer to be around positive and good energy. She refunded me my money which was the right thing to do. In the end she lost a customer and I happily went over to Under the Moon and had an amazing lunch and got to see the owners who I have known there for years.  If anyone is in bordentown check out Under the Moon and SANTIAGO makes some of the best desserts and even decorates the place by hand and love :) If you are gluten free go to Wildflower Baker ; they have some great food and dessert there. It's in Lawrenceville. Playa Bowls is another great one and they have toast there too as well as gluten free oats!! Watch out when PF gets a line,  the service is slow as molasses. She would have made up that lost sandwich with one or two visits from me and I was there a lot. I'll
Be happy to take my business elsewhere for how I was treated

Ok I went here after hearing from several girls I know about how great, fresh, and wonderful it is.  I'm sure the food is fresh, light, and delicious to some people but I have to totally disagree with anyone that calls it "healthy" as it certainly isn't.  They do offer lots and lots of nice looking desserts but everything on the menu, other than the soups, seems very heavy on the carbs, fats, and sugars here so I think some girls delude themselves that they are eating "healthy" here just to justify being able to order the super desserts as a "reward" for their "healthy" eating (if I ate this kind of food ratio often I would be huge!).  The menu is also a bit on the expensive side for the small portion sizes.  

They really didn't have anything I liked (I love meat but don't eat pig) but the soups were decent but not good enough for the price.  This is definitely a place for a "light" lunch.  Il Posto really just reminds me of a coffee shop that decided to throw in some sandwiches (but use some quality ingredients to make them a bit fancier).  The seating area is TINY and has very little space.  

I just find this is a place for dainty girls to eat and not men so I will never be back as it just isn't my type of food.  If you like this type of food and like light lunches this is certainly a place you might want to check out.  If I'm in this area I will be going to Pascal's Manale or Charlie's Steakhouse instead for my healthy food :)

This place looks quite cute from the street, but the service, clientele, and food destroy any possibilities it had of being a nice place. I went to dinner here with my best friend and boy friend on my birthday. We brought a nice bottle of wine and sat outside to share some gourmet pizzas. However, the table of people sitting next to us was so loud that we could not even her one another or ourselves when we were talking. (They had a giant bottle of wine--one of the ones that has two or three bottles in one--and a bottle of vodka on their table, but no food, for three people. They were dressed for clubbing, and seemed to think that they were already at the club.) In the nicest way I could think of, I kindly asked the loud folks if they would be willing to keep it down just a little bit so that we could hear one another talk. I apologized for bothering them and explained that I hoped that they could still have fun and a nice evening, just that we were having a little trouble hearing one another. I considered asking the waiter to do this for me, but thought that it would go over better if I asked directly, instead of asking the waiter to be my messenger. This clearly had no positive impact on the situation. Instantly, the group of loud folks starting jeering at us, calling us names (including profanities), taking our photos with their phones, and carrying on, as loudly as possible, about how they were outside and should be able to be as loud as they wanted. Eventually, we said something to our waiter, and he seemed to make friends with them and apologize for us having such an unreasonable request. I then went inside and said something to the manager who was oh so apologetic, but did nothing for us. In fact, he comped their bill because they were so inconvenienced--they went inside and complained about the fact that we asked them nicely to quiet down just a little bit. So, we ended up paying for our meal, while they did not, even though our meal was ruined. To make matters worse, the pizzas were expensive and the ingredients were of very low quality. The waiter kept raving about their freshly-made buffalo mozzarella, which had absolutely no flavor. I can honestly make much better pizzas (for a heck of a lot less money) at home. The place is cute, but the service and clientele are awful, the prices are expensive, and the food is mediocre. Save your money and head right around the corner to Gusto, which has great food at great prices. It's a lot less cute in terms of ambience, but at least the people who work their are nice.

My what a difference a little time makes. Was in the area with the kids and looked forward to another good trip to Pizza Perfect...Was sorely disappointed; Not only with the pizza (which was much worse than I remembered...the sauce was old, I think), but even more disappointed in the attitude of the people working there. It is purely amazing that managers and owners of businesses that deal with the public fail to instruct their employees on the absolute neccessity of good customer service in the age of immediate online reviews and social media. Astounding, really. 
So here's the deal:
The Kids spent a little time in the game room where my 10 year old daughter put 1 quarter in a game that took 2. She wanted her money back and hit the coin return lever, but nothing happened. She came to the table to tell me and I told her to tell the young lady at the counter...I was trying to teach her a lesson about asking for what you want and was certain she would experience a good lesson in customer service when she got her quarter back. T'was not to be. The girl at the counter said that since she only put 1 quarter in a 2 quarter game she could not get her money back unless she put another quarter in and pressed the coin return (Keep in mind that this was an older game that just starts without giving you the option the get your money back...But I digress). No biggie, no problem, I thought, I'll just put the other quarter in and let her play the game. So I put another quarter in, and...wait for it...nothing happened. I hit the coin return lever (remember, old game), and...wait for it...nothing happened. So now back to the counter to get 50 cents. No biggie, no problem, I thought, they will just give me the 2 quarters and we'll be on our way. Not yet...Now I have to face the same girl at the counter who proceeds to say, "Well, did anyone else play the game between the time your daughter put her quarter in and the time you did (maybe 30 seconds)? No I said, there is no one else in there (the restaurant was nearly empty...I wonder why? There I go again: Digressing.) "I just need my 50 cents", I said. Finally she grudgingly hands it over, with an attitude. I decided to give her a little construcvtive feedback, so I say, "Hey, you probably should have just given her her quarter back in the first place. I would have been good customer service, you know." "Well", she says, "that's not our policy." Really?! She pulled the old, "not our policy" over a cool 25 cents. Brilliant.
"Ok", I say, "you have lost a customer as a result of your 'policy', be sure to let your manager know we won't be back." I get the kids from the game room to leave and as we're leaving I notice the girl talking to a slightly older guy in a plain white tee behind the counter and he's looking at me like I just took a dump in the middle of his restaurant. Oh great, I think, a 20 year old night manager at a pizza joint on a Monday: The very definition of 'a big fish in a small pond'. I look at him and say, "Great customer service you have here. We will not be back, and rest assured I will be writing some online reviews of how poorly we were treated in your establishment." 
"Well, that's against our policy, so you can write all the reviews you want." 
"OK, I'll be sure to do that. What's your name?"
"Matt", he says. 
"Great, I'll be sure to mention you." 
So there you go Matt. You've been noted and we will not ever be back. 
Promises kept. That's MY policy.

Boy oh boy, what an exciting  experience at my local Burger King today! I haven't been back to this BK on a while since my wife and I went for milkshakes and as we ordered them we could hear an employee in the background shouting "nah bruh, no milkshakes". Needless to say we took our business to sonic that evening and evenings since then for our milkshake needs. 

But today, when I pulled up around 1:35 to order a quick bite to eat I was "greeted" I guess you could call it by easily the most soft spoken person to have lived in the 21st century. I ordered my #5 just the sandwich and a large fries and when I concluded ordering she very boldly stated "that's it?". Why yes today in fact I am not going to have anything else that could possibly make your job any harder. She tells me "aight they Gona help you at the 2nd window". 

Cool beans food time right. Here is where it gets interesting. As I pull forward through the charbroiled smoke cloud of doom I'm greeted by a very nice young lady whom I give my payment to. As I look down for half a second to glance at my phone in my lap, shame on me for distracted driving right. Out of nowhere I hear "HOW YOU DOING SIR, MY NAMES CRYSTAL, IM A NEW EMPLOYEE HERE, WOULD TOU FILL THIS SURVEY OUT TO WIN A FREE SANDWICH?", shouted at me as a 4th grader would who try as they might can't remember their lines for the school play so they need to shout them as loud as possible when they enter their frontal cortex. She manages to somehow squeeze her way between the nice calm young lady taking care of my order and the window like an unwanted popcorn kernel between two poor unsuspecting teeth. "Crystal", now hands me a crumpled blank piece of receipt paper one side being the typical "free whopper, let us know what you think on on side and the other with the name "CRyStal" written in yellow highlighter In what appears to be a form of calligraphy used by the the blind and illiterate. I said " I'll give it a shot, knocking I would probably just crumple it up and throw it away." But now she repeats herself a second time much like a child who doesn't get enough attention at home and feels the need to repeat themselves to ensure they are heard, and I decided to hang on to it as I observed her wearing the only backwards hat in the restaurant. 

She must be important right. I can only make that assumption by the stand out uniform she was wearing, the 4x sized jacket and the backwards hat and the unbelievably low sagging pants. Like pants sagging so low you should just take your pants off as they aren't serving the engineered purpose as pants. Anyways she begins to turn her back to resume bothering any other poor person whom she might have to encounter during the day. I felt as though I was born again during my visit after she left my general vicinity. So almost time to get my food yay! Now she goes to bother someone else and says "I can't deal with y'all today, in what seemed to be a joking manner" and then I hear her say "WHAT IS THIS SOURDOUGH" it couldn't be, my worst fear, the distracting,loud,obnoxious, cringey, malibu's most wanted looking individual was going to handle my food. At any rate someone from around the corner says "that's his". Ah yes, the pinnacle of my experience when I get to have my food and leave. Shortly thereafter a lady in a blue polo come from around the corner with a bag and a receipt. The same receipt that CRyStal gave me eairler with the survey on the back, OH BOY! As she's handing my my brown sack of potential sadness she says "that was my fault" in a very monotone unsure voice. But alas, my dear lady in the blue polo, CRyStal appears to be at the fault of society for lacking some social etiquette and dress standards. 

My hamburger was pretty good. Burger King has the best French fries of all the he French fries to ever be fried. My today could have used a dash more salt, but still pretty good.

Service here is lacking and needs a lot of work and acccountability. If I wanted to be bothered in such a way I would choose to spend time around children. Which I don't have any of because I hate them. 

If Bummer King brings back the lucky charms milkshake and can assure we can order and receive it during hours of operation I will consider bringing my business back.

I never understood how some restaurants would get so many mixed reviews ; how some people would rate it 5 stars and others only 1. That is , until I went to VCibo last night . We decided to go because it is a brand new restaurant right down the street in an area seriously lacking in good dining options . I read the reviews here and on Trip Advisor and although there were only 5 total , they were all great and all gave the place 5 stars , so it was with great anticipation that we headed over . The restaurant itself is quite charming but very small ; perhaps only 10 tables max . My friend and I felt fortunate to get the last open table and it wasn't even six o'clock yet . Our server was prompt and friendly and we ordered the Chianti from their list of wines on tap. Then the trouble started . We were served bread and oil and the bread was minuscule and roughly cut; cold and pretty tasteless- definitely nothing to write about .  The menu was pretty limited but there seemed to be some good choices . After inquiring about the Eggplant Parmesan , and being told that " everyone loved it ", I decided to give it a try as it's one of my favorite dishes . My friend decided to forgo her diet and order the lasagna bolognese. The dishes arrived promptly but I was dismayed to see that all I got was a small round stack of eggplant with some spaghetti on the side . I was surprised at how little it was considering that they charged $14.95 for it . My friends' lasagna was also on the small side but worse , most of it was completely burnt. I tasted my dish and was even more disappointed . There was no sauce whatsoever - All I could taste were breadcrumbs - no other flavor to it at all and it was lukewarm to boot . My friend was also dissatisfied with her dish but wound up eating a small amount of it anyway . To her credit , when the server saw I wasn't eating my eggplant she inquired and agreed that it didn't look like what was normally served and offered to get it " fixed". A few minutes later she came back with what looked like the same eggplant but with a spoonful of sauce on top . I took the top layer off and saw that there was virtually no cheese on it at all; tasted it and it was still very disappointing . By this time , the owner/ manager ? came over and said that they had a new chef in the kitchen and obviously he wasn't doing a good job . She offered to bring me an order of cheese lasagna to try ; I was hesitant given my friends' disappointment with HER lasagna , but I was hungry and figured I'd give it a try . Well , it was pretty terrible ; the noodles were hard and again, there was very little cheese , but for one piece of mozzarella on top that tasted off . It was also a small portion but considering how bad it tasted, that was ok. The server seemed pretty distressed and again cited the chef as being to blame . Again the owner came by and apologized but there wasn't really anything else to do . She didn't charge us for either of our meals which certainly was fair since we barely ate anything . We each had two glasses of wine , which they DID charge us for - something that I think they should have probably offered to us as well ( at least ONE of the glasses)  given all that we went through and especially because all we heard was how terrible the chef was and how difficult it is to find a good chef - did we really need to hear all that ? I didn't dare try a dessert for fear of having to return that as well . But the biggest kicker of all was , as we were getting ready to leave , the table next to us was served lasagna bolognese as well . I couldn't believe what I was seeing ! It looked like it came from a completely different restaurant ! It was a large portion and looked like it was fresh out of the oven ; smothered in sauce and cheese- it looked delicious . I called the owner over to inquire how that dish looked so completely different than ours and she told me that she just fired the chef and made THAT lasagna herself ! That was so disturbing . I mean, good for THAT customer , but we were still seriously disappointed. Where was she or someone watching when our food was presented by the chef ? It should have never left the kitchen the way it did . Sorry - I would have loved to give this place a great review - it's new so perhaps they'll work out the kinks at some point , but until they do , I think I'll make the trip to Pia's in Gulfport where I'm certain to get an excellent eggplant Parmesan and pretty much everything else .

Never again.  I am a long time patron of this restaurant.  I always liked it there.  But, tonight, two of us ordered entrées...  By the time our entrées arrived, we already ate the few garlic bread, or rolls, or knots, or whatever they want to call their precious valuable things.  We asked for more rolls or bread for our meals.  We nicely made it clear we were OK with simple bread.  Didn't have to be the valuable rolls or knots.  We were told it was in the oven.  OK, great..  The two of us held off eating our meals, thinking the bread was on it's way.  We are both Italian.  We eat bread with our pasta.  Sorry about that.  We waited.  15 minutes later, we asked about the bread.  The waitress said she was trying to get us more bread, but "they are very strict" about giving more bread.  Really?  Wait..  Can't have more bread in an Italian restaurant?   We were willing to pay the $2 or $3 for a few more little rolls...  that probably cost 25 cents to make..  whatever you think they're worth.  But, no.  Not gonna happen.  They are too strict..  OK.  No problem.  We won't be coming back.  We have very strict convictions, too.  If you have been to this restaurant, you may have had good experiences there.  Us too..  But, when you have that one unacceptable experience, it is just a total turn off.  After an experience like that, why would you go back, when there are so many other restaurants in the area?  I just don't get it.  And I don't need it explained to me.  I am happy to go elsewhere, and I'll certainly make sure to tell my friends to do the same.
